name: Context Menu Manager
description: View, disable and enable entries in the Windows right-click menu
help: Lists the entries of the classic right-click menu for files, folders, folder background, desktop and drives: commands added by apps (such as “Open with Code”) and shell extensions (such as archive tools).

Turning an entry off hides it without deleting anything: commands get the LegacyDisable value Windows understands, and shell extensions are added to Windows' list of blocked extensions. Turning it back on undoes exactly that.
Before every change, an undo file (.reg) is saved; double-click it to restore that entry. Use “Undo files” to open the folder.
Entries installed for all users and every shell extension need administrator rights. If a change is refused, run ToolForge as administrator.
On Windows 11, “Classic right-click menu” shows the full menu directly instead of behind “Show more options”. Changes to shell extensions and the classic menu take effect after restarting Explorer.
